questions.question:
Which products are formed in the chlor-alkali process when electricity is passed through an aqueous sodium chloride solution?

NaCl(aq) + H₂O(I) → Products
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**NaOH + H2 + Cl2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **chlor-alkali process** involves the electrolysis of an **aqueous sodium chloride (NaCl) solution**, also known as brine.
 
• When electricity is passed through the brine, it decomposes into three main products: **sodium hydroxide (NaOH)**, **chlorine gas (Cl2)**, and **hydrogen gas (H2)**.
 
• The reactions occurring at the electrodes are:
 
 
• **Cathode (Reduction):** 2H₂O + 2e⁻ → H₂ + 2OH⁻
 
• **Anode (Oxidation):** 2Cl⁻ → Cl₂ + 2e⁻
 
 
 
• The **sodium ions (Na⁺)** in the solution combine with the **hydroxide ions (OH⁻)** to form **sodium hydroxide (NaOH)**.
 
• The products **NaOH, H2, and Cl2** are commercially valuable. **Sodium hydroxide** is used in the manufacture of paper, soap, and detergents. **Chlorine** is used for disinfecting water, in the production of PVC, and in the manufacture of various chemicals. **Hydrogen** is used in hydrogenation processes and as a fuel.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **NaCl + H2**__

 __
 
• This option is incorrect because **sodium chloride (NaCl)** is the reactant, not the product, in the chlor-alkali process.
 
• **Hydrogen gas (H2)** is indeed produced, but not sodium chloride.
 
 
 
• **NaHCO3 + Cl2**__
 __
 
• This option is incorrect because **sodium bicarbonate (NaHCO3)** is not produced in the chlor-alkali process.
 
• **Chlorine gas (Cl2)** is produced, but not sodium bicarbonate.
 
 
 
• **H2 + O2**__
 
 
• This option is incorrect because **oxygen gas (O2)** is not produced in the chlor-alkali process.
 
• **Hydrogen gas (H2)** is produced, but not oxygen.

questions.question: A series of compounds in which the same functional group substitutes for hydrogen in a carbon chain is called _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**homologous series**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **homologous series** is a group of organic compounds that have a similar general formula and possess similar chemical properties.
 
• In a homologous series, each successive member differs by a **-CH2- unit**.
 
• The members of a homologous series are called **homologues**.
 
• Homologous series exhibit a gradual change in **physical properties** such as boiling point, melting point, and density.
 
• Examples of homologous series include **alkanes, alkenes, and alkynes**.
 
• One notable characteristic is that the **functional group** remains the same throughout the series.
 
• Homologous series are important in organic chemistry because they help in the systematic study and prediction of properties of organic compounds.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Isomers**__

 __
 
• **Isomers** are compounds that have the same molecular formula but different structural arrangements.
 
• Isomers can be classified into **structural isomers** and **stereoisomers**.
 
• Structural isomers have different connectivity of atoms, while stereoisomers have the same connectivity but differ in spatial arrangement.
 
 
 
• **Isochores**__
 __
 
• **Isochores** are regions of DNA with a high degree of uniformity in base composition.
 
• They are significant in the field of genetics and genomics.
 
 
 
• **Isobars**__
 
 
• **Isobars** are atoms of different chemical elements that have the same number of nucleons.
 
• Isobars differ in chemical properties because they have different atomic numbers.

questions.question: Find the compound interest on Rs. 13,000 in 2 years at 4% p.a., interest compounded yearly.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Effective **Rate of Interest** for 2 years at 4% = x + y + (xy/100)

⇒ 4 + 4 + (4 × 4)/100 = 8.16%

**Compound Interest** = 8.16% of ₹13,000

⇒ 130 × 8.16 = ₹1060.80

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1060.80.**

**__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/70dd1295964e09110cb578cae57135989da1ae7e43c32d5b91a161d42894c408.png] 

**Given:** Principal (P) = ₹13,000, Rate (R) = 4%, Time (n) = 2 years

**Formula Used:** Amount (A) = P(1 + R/100)ⁿ; CI = A − P

⇒ A = 13000(1 + 4/100)²

⇒ A = 13000(104/100) × (104/100)

⇒ A = 130 × 1.04 × 104 = 14060.80

⇒ CI = 14060.80 − 13000

⇒ CI = ₹1060.80

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1060.80.**

**__Additional Information__**

Successive Percentage Method

Compound interest is essentially the result of **successive percentage increases** on the principal amount.

Difference between SI and CI

For 2 years, the difference between **CI and SI** is given by the formula: D = P(R/100)².

Compounding Half-Yearly

If interest is **compounded half-yearly**, the rate is halved (R/2) and the time is doubled (2n).

questions.question: The average temperature for Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, and Thursday was 48ºC, and for Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, and Friday was 46ºC. If the temperature on Monday was 42ºC, find the temperature on Friday.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Net difference between **Monday** and **Friday** = Number of days × (Difference in averages)

⇒ **Monday** − **Friday** = 4 × (48 − 46) = 4 × 2 = 8°C

⇒ 42 − **Friday** = 8

⇒ **Friday** = 42 − 8 = 34°C

**∴ The correct answer is 34°C.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/59073e44e9ff1654d4f73c9fbbf505a31cafa33bb1df6f532b123e2644dddd41.png] 

**Given:**

Average (Mon, Tue, Wed, Thu) = 48°C

Average (Tue, Wed, Thu, Fri) = 46°C

Temperature on Monday = 42°C

**Formula Used:**

Sum of observations = Average × Number of observations

**Calculations:**

⇒ Sum(Mon + Tue + Wed + Thu) = 48 × 4 = 192°C

⇒ Sum(Tue + Wed + Thu + Fri) = 46 × 4 = 184°C

⇒ (Mon + Tue + Wed + Thu) − (Tue + Wed + Thu + Fri) = 192 − 184

⇒ Mon − Fri = 8°C

⇒ 42 − Fri = 8

⇒ Fri = 42 − 8 = 34°C

**∴ The correct answer is 34°C.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average of a Group

Average = (Sum of all observations) ÷ (Total number of observations).

Deviation Method

If one member is replaced, the change in sum = (Number of members) × (Change in Average).

Temperature Problems

In overlapping day series, common days cancel out when subtracting the total sums of the two sets.</p

questions.question: Which statement is NOT true for magnetic field lines?

options.text: Magnetic field lines are not closed curves.
No two field lines are found to cross each other.
Inside the magnet, the direction of field lines is from its south pole to its north pole.
The relative strength of the magnetic field is shown by the degree of closeness of the field lines.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Magnetic field lines are not closed curves.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Magnetic field lines** are indeed **closed curves**. They start from the **north pole** of a magnet and end at the **south pole**, forming continuous loops inside and outside the magnet.
 
• **No two field lines** are found to cross each other. If they did, it would mean that the magnetic field has two directions at that point, which is not possible.
 
• Inside the magnet, the direction of field lines is from its **south pole to its north pole**. This is part of the continuous loop of the magnetic field lines.
 
• The relative **strength of the magnetic field** is shown by the degree of **closeness of the field lines**. The closer the lines, the stronger the magnetic field in that region.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **No two field lines cross each other**__

 __
 
• If two magnetic field lines crossed, it would imply that the magnetic field has two different directions at the same point, which is impossible.
 
 
 
• **Inside the magnet, the direction of field lines is from south to north**__
 __
 
• This indicates that magnetic field lines form closed loops, going from north to south outside the magnet and from south to north inside the magnet.
 
 
 
• **The relative strength of the magnetic field**__
 
 
• The closeness of magnetic field lines indicates the strength of the magnetic field; closer lines mean a stronger field.

questions.question: In an election between two candidates, one got 55% of the total valid votes, and 20% of the votes were invalid. If the total number of votes was 7500, the number of valid votes that the other candidate got was:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Total Votes** = 7500

**Valid Votes** = 80% of 7500 = 6000

Winner gets 55%, so **Other Candidate** gets 45% of valid votes.

Other Candidate = 45% of 6000 = 0.45 × 6000 = 2700

**∴ The correct answer is 2700 votes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9076232998c42f74065206d73a3977e5182e2ccd28a37a9e471dddde464def6d.png] 

**Given:**

Total votes = 7500

Invalid votes = 20%

Winner candidate share = 55% of valid votes

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total Valid votes = 7500 × (100 − 20)%

⇒ Total Valid votes = 7500 × 80/100 = 6000

⇒ Other candidate share = 100% − 55% = 45% of valid votes

⇒ Votes for other candidate = 45/100 × 6000

⇒ Votes for other candidate = 45 × 60 = 2700

**∴ The correct answer is 2700 votes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Percentage Base Change

Always identify the correct base for percentages. In elections, candidate percentages are usually calculated on **Valid Votes**, not **Total Votes**, unless specified otherwise.

Successive Percentage Shortcut

Result = Total × (Valid % / 100) × (Candidate % / 100). Here, 7500 × 0.80 × 0.45 = 2700.</p

questions.question: The population of a town is 1,76,400. If it increases at the rate of 5% per annum, then what will be its population 2 years hence?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Growth rate = 5% → Multiplying factor = 1 + 5/100 = 1.05

Successive increase for 2 years = (1.05)² = 1.1025

New Population = 1,76,400 × 1.1025 = 1,94,481

**∴ The correct answer is 1,94,481.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c72015cbae60b3c369613e96626f4cee4fade83bf23d6855dba909c1d4f9a997.png] 

**Given:**

Present Population (P) = 1,76,400

Rate of Increase (R) = 5%

Time period (n) = 2 years

**Formula Used:**

Population after n years = P × (1 + R/100)ⁿ

**Calculations:**

⇒ Population = 1,76,400 × (1 + 5/100)²

⇒ Population = 1,76,400 × (105/100) × (105/100)

⇒ Population = 1,76,400 × (21/20) × (21/20)

⇒ Population = 1,76,400 × (441/400)

⇒ Population = 441 × 441

⇒ Population = 1,94,481

**∴ The correct answer is 1,94,481.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Population Decrease

If the population decreases at rate R, the formula becomes: P × (1 − R/100)ⁿ.

Successive Percentage Method

For two years, the net percentage change can be calculated as x + y + (xy/100). Here, 5 + 5 + (25/100) = 10.25%.

Finding Previous Population

To find the population n years ago, the formula is: Population / (1 + R/100)ⁿ.</p

questions.question: By selling 8 oranges for ₹40, a man loses 20%. How many should he sell for ₹30 to gain 20% in the transaction?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Using the price-quantity-percentage relation: **(Price₁) ÷ (Quantity₁ × Selling%₁) = (Price₂) ÷ (Quantity₂ × Selling%₂)**

Here, Selling%₁ = 100% − Loss% = 100% − 20% = 80%

And, Selling%₂ = 100% + Gain% = 100% + 20% = 120%

Let the required quantity of oranges be **x**.

⇒ 40 ÷ (8 × 80) = 30 ÷ (x × 120)

⇒ 40 ÷ 640 = 30 ÷ (120x) ⇒ 1 ÷ 16 = 1 ÷ (4x) ⇒ 4x = 16 ⇒ **x = 4**

**∴ The correct answer is 4.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Selling Price (SP₁) of 8 oranges = **₹40**

Loss percentage = **20%**

Desired Gain percentage = **20%**

New Total Selling Price (SP₂) = **₹30**

**Formulas:**

Cost Price (CP) = SP × 100 ÷ (100 − Loss%)

New Selling Price (SP) = CP × (100 + Gain%) ÷ 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/fea9efa1b9d7c33488b3a476c021d2750eabcab5961dfe20dfaaaa3ff5ef8e56.png] 

**Steps:**

⇒ SP of 1 orange in first case = 40 ÷ 8 = **₹5**

⇒ Since there is a 20% loss, CP of 1 orange = 5 × 100 ÷ (100 − 20) = 5 × 100 ÷ 80 = **₹6.25**

⇒ CP of 8 oranges = 8 × 6.25 = **₹50**

⇒ To gain 20%, SP of 8 oranges should be = 50 × (100 + 20) ÷ 100 = 50 × 1.2 = **₹60**

⇒ If 8 oranges are sold for ₹60 to get 20% gain, then the number of oranges to be sold for ₹30 is:

⇒ Quantity for ₹30 = (8 ÷ 60) × 30 = **4 oranges**

**∴ The correct answer is 4.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Unitary Method in Price and Quantity

For a constant total value, the quantity sold is inversely proportional to the price per unit. When the required profit increases, the selling price per unit increases, which means fewer items must be sold for the same amount of money.

questions.question: The work done by a constant force acting on a body is ______
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**either positive or negative**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The work done by a **constant force** on a body depends on the **direction of the force** relative to the direction of the **displacement** of the body.
 
• If the force is in the same direction as the displacement, the work done is **positive**.
 
• If the force is in the opposite direction to the displacement, the work done is **negative**.
 
• When the force and displacement are perpendicular to each other, the work done is **zero**.
 
• Therefore, the work done by a constant force can be **positive, negative, or zero**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **always zero**__

 __
 
• This option is incorrect because the work done by a constant force is not always zero.
 
• Work done can be zero only if the force is perpendicular to the displacement.
 
 
 
• **always positive**__
 __
 
• This option is incorrect because the work done by a constant force is not always positive.
 
• Work done is positive only if the force is in the same direction as the displacement.
 
 
 
• **always negative**__
 
 
• This option is incorrect because the work done by a constant force is not always negative.
 
• Work done is negative only if the force is in the opposite direction to the displacement.

questions.question: The kind of energy possessed by a moving body by virtue of its motion is _______
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**kinetic energy**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kinetic energy** is the energy possessed by a body due to its **motion**.
 
• It is calculated using the formula: **KE = 1/2 mv²**, where **m** is the mass of the object and **v** is its velocity.
 
• All moving objects have kinetic energy, regardless of their direction of motion.
 
• Examples include a moving car, a flying airplane, a flowing river, and even the particles in a gas or liquid.
 
• **Conversion** of energy: Kinetic energy can be converted into other forms of energy, such as potential energy, thermal energy, etc.
 
• It is a **scalar quantity** and always has a positive value.
 
• The SI unit of kinetic energy is the **joule (J)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Electromagnetic energy**__

 __
 
• **Electromagnetic energy** is a form of energy that is reflected or emitted in the form of electrical and magnetic waves that can travel through space.
 
• Examples include **light, radio waves, and X-rays**.
 
 
 
• **Nuclear energy**__
 __
 
• **Nuclear energy** is the energy released during nuclear reactions, such as **fission or fusion**.
 
• It is used in **nuclear power plants** and **nuclear weapons**.
 
 
 
• **Potential energy**__
 
 
• **Potential energy** is the energy possessed by an object due to its position or configuration.
 
• Examples include a **stretched spring** or an object held at a height.

questions.question: Select the term which is not an identity.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

An **identity** must hold true for **all values** of the variables involved.

Test **option 3** with **a = 1, b = 1**:

LHS = (1 + 1)² = 2² = 4 | RHS = 1² + 1² = 2

Since **4 ≠ 2**, the equation is not an identity.

**∴ The correct answer is (a + b)² = a² + b².**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Four mathematical expressions to identify which is **not an identity**.

**Concept:** An **identity** is an equality that remains true regardless of the values chosen for its variables. An **equation** that is true only for specific values is not an identity.

⇒ Option 1: (a + b)² = a² + b² + 2ab (Standard Algebraic Identity)

⇒ Option 2: (a + 1)(a + 2) = a × a + a × 2 + 1 × a + 1 × 2 = a² + 3a + 2 (True for all 'a')

⇒ Option 4: (a − b)² = a² + b² − 2ab (Standard Algebraic Identity)

⇒ Option 3: (a + b)² = a² + b²

⇒ Expanding LHS: a² + b² + 2ab

⇒ Comparing with RHS: a² + b² + 2ab ≠ a² + b² (unless a × b = 0)

**∴ The correct answer is (a + b)² = a² + b².**

**__Additional Information__**

Algebraic Identity

An equality relation A = B, such that A and B contain some variables and A and B produce the same value as each other regardless of what values are substituted for the variables.

Difference of Squares

A very common identity used in simplification is (a + b)(a − b) = a² − b².

Conditional Equations

Equations like x + 2 = 5 are only true for x = 3, hence they are not identities.</p

questions.question:
Which of the following statements regarding saturated and unsaturated carbon compounds is correct?

Statement I: Saturated carbon compounds are hydrocarbons where carbon atoms are connected by single covalent bonds.

Statement II: Unsaturated carbon compounds are hydrocarbons where carbon atoms are connected by single covalent bonds.

options.text: Neither statement I nor II is correct.
Both statements I and II are correct.

questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Only statement I is correct**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Saturated carbon compounds** are hydrocarbons where carbon atoms are connected by **single covalent bonds**.
 
• These compounds are typically **alkanes**.
 
• **Unsaturated carbon compounds** are hydrocarbons where carbon atoms are connected by **double or triple covalent bonds**.
 
• These compounds include **alkenes** (with double bonds) and **alkynes** (with triple bonds).
 
• Statement I correctly describes saturated carbon compounds.
 
• Statement II incorrectly describes unsaturated carbon compounds as having single covalent bonds, which is characteristic of saturated compounds.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Saturated hydrocarbons**__

 __
 
• These are **aliphatic hydrocarbons** like **methane, ethane, and propane**.
 
• They are generally **less reactive** than unsaturated hydrocarbons.
 
 
 
• **Unsaturated hydrocarbons**__
 
 
• These compounds include **ethene (ethylene)** and **ethyne (acetylene)**.
 
• They are more **reactive** due to the presence of multiple bonds.

II. Some person or people migrate in response to the adverse effects of climate change, natural disasters, or other environmental factors.

options.text: Both I and II are possible reasons
Neither I nor II is a possible reason.
Only I is a possible reason.
Only II is a possible reason.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both I and II are possible reasons**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Migration** refers to the movement of a person or people from one country, locality, or place of residence to settle in another.
 
• **Reason I** explains that migration occurs due to various factors such as the search for work, economic opportunities, joining family, or studying. Additionally, people may migrate to escape conflict, persecution, terrorism, or human rights violations.
 
• **Reason II** highlights that migration can also be driven by environmental factors such as the adverse effects of climate change, natural disasters, or other environmental challenges.
 
• Both reasons are valid and encompass a wide range of factors that contribute to migration.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Reason I**__

 __
 
• People often migrate for **economic opportunities** such as better job prospects and higher wages.
 
• **Family reunification** is another important factor where people move to join family members already settled in another region.
 
• Many students migrate to pursue **higher education** and enhance their skills.

questions.question: In Δ PQR, ∠Q = ∠R and QR = 12 cm, PR= 10 cm and PS be the altitude, then the length of PS is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Since **∠Q = ∠R**, Δ PQR is an **Isosceles triangle** with **PQ = PR = 10 cm**.

In an isosceles triangle, the **altitude PS** bisects the base **QR** → **QS = SR = 12 ÷ 2 = 6 cm**.

Using **Pythagorean triplet (6, 8, 10)** in right-angled Δ PSQ: **PS² + 6² = 10²**.

**PS = √(100 − 36) = √64 = 8 cm**.

**∴ The correct answer is 8 cm.**

**__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2f9f866df1c15ed2eb69ae63f6815199f20d1422ae12580fc9e34a4606e59695.png] 

**Given:** QR = 12 cm, PR = 10 cm, ∠Q = ∠R.

**Formula Used:** Pythagoras Theorem: Hypotenuse² = Base² + Perpendicular².

⇒ In Δ PQR, as ∠Q = ∠R, sides opposite to equal angles are equal ∴ **PQ = PR = 10 cm**.

⇒ **PS** is the altitude to the base **QR** of an isosceles triangle, so it bisects **QR**.

⇒ **QS = SR = QR ÷ 2 = 12 ÷ 2 = 6 cm**.

⇒ In right Δ PSQ, **PQ² = PS² + QS²**.

⇒ 10² = PS² + 6²

⇒ 100 = PS² + 36

⇒ PS² = 64

⇒ **PS = 8 cm**.

**∴ The correct answer is 8 cm.**

**__Additional Information__**

Isosceles Triangle Properties

The altitude from the vertex between equal sides to the base bisects the base and the vertex angle.

Pythagorean Triplets

Common triplets like (3, 4, 5), (6, 8, 10), and (5, 12, 13) help solve right-triangle problems instantly.

Area of Triangle

Area = 1/2 × Base × Height. For this triangle, Area = 1/2 × 12 × 8 = 48 cm².</p

Total Work = (6M + 8B) × 10 = (12B + 8B) × 10 = 200B

questions.question: The inverse ratio of 1 : 2 : 3 is:

For a ratio **a : b : c**, the **inverse ratio** is **(b×c) : (a×c) : (a×b)**.

Given ratio → 1 : 2 : 3

⇒ 6 : 3 : 2

Inverse Ratio Property

The **inverse ratio** (or reciprocal ratio) of a : b is 1/a : 1/b, which simplifies to b : a.

Compound Ratio

questions.question: The mode of the observations 20, 23, 25, 30, 20, 31, 32, 35, 20, 41, 42, 43, 20 and 20 is:

**Mode** is the value that appears most frequently in a data set.

List frequencies: 23(1), 25(1), 30(1), 31(1), 32(1), 35(1), 41(1), 42(1), 43(1), and **20(5)**.

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Observations = 20, 23, 25, 30, 20, 31, 32, 35, 20, 41, 42, 43, 20, 20

⇒ Frequency of other terms = 1 each

⇒ Maximum frequency is associated with the term 20.

⇒ Mode = 20

**∴ The correct answer is 20.**

**__Additional Information__**

Empirical Formula

The relationship between Mean, Median, and Mode is given by: Mode = 3 × Median − 2 × Mean.

Bimodal and Multimodal

If two or more values have the same maximum frequency, the distribution is called bimodal or multimodal.

Central Tendency

Mode is one of the three measures of central tendency, primarily used for categorical data to find the most popular item.</p

questions.question: What is the SI unit of momentum?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**kg m s⁻¹**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Momentum** is a fundamental concept in **physics** that describes the quantity of motion an object has.
 
• It is a vector quantity, meaning it has both **magnitude** and **direction**.
 
• The formula for momentum (**p**) is given by **p = m × v**, where **m** is the mass of the object and **v** is its velocity.
 
• The **SI unit** (International System of Units) for mass is **kilogram (kg)** and for velocity is **meters per second (m/s)**.
 
• Therefore, the SI unit of momentum is derived from these two units, resulting in **kg m s⁻¹**.
 
• Understanding momentum is crucial in various fields of **physics** and **engineering**, such as in the study of collisions and conservation laws.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 __
 
• This unit is used in the context of viscosity in fluid dynamics, specifically the **dynamic viscosity**.
 
• Dynamic viscosity is a measure of a fluid's resistance to flow.
 
 
 
• **kg m**__
 __
 
• This combination of units does not correspond to a standard physical quantity in the SI system.
 
 
 
• **kg m s**__
 
 
• This unit is incorrect because it does not account for the squared time unit required for velocity.

questions.question: If 3 : 6 :: 6 : a, what is the value of a?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__
In a **continued proportion** a : b :: b : c, the **product of extremes** equals the **product of means**.

Given 3 : 6 :: 6 : a

Product of extremes = 3 × a

Product of means = 6 × 6 = 36

a = 36 ÷ 3 = 12

**∴ The correct answer is 12.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** 3 : 6 :: 6 : a

**Formula Used:** If w : x :: y : z, then w/x = y/z.
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/53e016c9e57ba1537f6bc9192fc731def3094b0bb6565dd5a7015ff73a29e4ad.png] 
⇒ 3 / 6 = 6 / a

⇒ 1 / 2 = 6 / a

⇒ a = 6 × 2

⇒ a = 12

**∴ The correct answer is 12.**

**__Additional Information__**

Mean Proportional

If a, b, c are in continued proportion, then b is the mean proportional between a and c, where b² = ac or b = √(ac).

Third Proportional

In the proportion a : b :: b : c, the term c is called the third proportional to a and b, calculated as c = b² ÷ a.

Fourth Proportional

In the proportion a : b :: c : d, the term d is the fourth proportional, calculated as d = (b × c) ÷ a.</p

questions.question: Accumulation of which substance in our muscles during sudden activity causes cramps?

• **Lactic acid** accumulates in muscles during intense exercise or sudden activity.

• The buildup of **lactic acid** leads to a condition known as **muscle acidosis**, causing cramps and fatigue.
 
• This process is typically a temporary response to high-intensity exercise.

questions.question: Which of the following equations is true, when two objects A and B of masses M and m are separated by a distance d, F is the force of attraction between them and G is the universal gravitational constant?

__
 
• The formula **F = G(M × m)/(d²)** represents **Newton's Law of Universal Gravitation**.
 
• According to this law, the **force of attraction** between two objects is directly proportional to the **product of their masses** (M and m).
 
• The force is also **inversely proportional** to the **square of the distance** (d) between the two objects.
 
• **G** is the **universal gravitational constant**, which has a value of approximately **6.674 × 10^-11 N(m/kg)²**.
 
• This formula is crucial in understanding the **gravitational interactions** between objects, from small particles to astronomical bodies.

• F = G(M)/(d²): This formula is incorrect because it does not include the mass of object B (m).
 
• F = G(1)/(d²): This formula is incorrect because it does not include the masses of either object.
 
• F = G(M × m)/(d): This formula is incorrect because the force is inversely proportional to the square of the distance (d²), not just the distance (d).
 
 
 
• **Important Points**__
 
 
• **Newton's Law of Universal Gravitation** is fundamental in physics and astronomy.
 
• This law helps in calculating the **gravitational forces** between celestial bodies, which is essential for understanding their **orbits** and **movements**.
 
• The **universal gravitational constant** (G) was first measured by **Henry Cavendish** in 1798.

• Here, the **mass** (m) of the rice bag is **10 kg**.
 
• The **acceleration due to gravity** (g) is given as **10 ms⁻²**.
 
• So, the force exerted is: **F = 10 kg × 10 ms⁻² = 100 N**.
 
• The **displacement** (d) of the rice bag is **2 meters** (the height at which the bag is lifted).
 
• Therefore, the work done by the worker is: **W = F × d = 100 N × 2 m = 200 J**.
 
• Hence, the correct answer is **200 J**.

questions.question: The age of a mother six years ago was six times the age of her daughter, at that time. Three years hence, the mother will be thrice as old as her daughter. What is the difference between the present age of the mother and her daughter?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Ratio 6 years ago (M:D) = 6 : 1 (Difference = 5 units)

Ratio 3 years hence (M:D) = 3 : 1 = 6 : 2 (Difference = 4 units)

Equating differences: Ratio1 × 4 → 24 : 4 | Ratio2 × 5 → 30 : 10

Change in units = 30 − 24 = 6 units → Total years gap = 6 + 3 = 9 years

1 unit = 9/6 = 1.5 years | Age difference = 20 units × 1.5 = 30 years

**∴ The correct answer is 30 years.**

**__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/dd84c15927863b7a92cc8ccc77c63650ef7913fac74e92b216b24d47b1f1b630.png] 

Let **daughter age** 6 years ago be x and **mother age** be 6x.

Present ages: Daughter = x + 6, Mother = 6x + 6

Ages 3 years hence: Daughter = x + 9, Mother = 6x + 9

⇒ 6x + 9 = 3 × (x + 9)

⇒ 6x + 9 = 3x + 27

⇒ 3x = 18

⇒ x = 6

⇒ Mother age 6 yrs ago = 6 × 6 = 36; Daughter age 6 yrs ago = 6

⇒ Age difference = 36 − 6 = 30 years

**∴ The correct answer is 30 years.**

**__Additional Information__**

Constant Difference Property

The **age difference** between two individuals always remains constant throughout their lives, regardless of the number of years passed.

Ratio Balancing

To solve age problems using ratios, multiply the ratios such that the **numerical difference** between the ratio parts of the two people becomes equal in both time periods.</p

questions.question: A change of state directly from gas to solid without changing into liquid state is called:

• This phase transition is the reverse of **sublimation**, which is the transition from a solid to a gas.
 
• An example of deposition is the formation of **frost** on cold surfaces from water vapor in the air.
 
• In **physical chemistry** and **material science**, deposition is a process used to create thin films or coatings on surfaces.
 
• Deposition is utilized in **manufacturing processes** such as **chemical vapor deposition (CVD)** and **physical vapor deposition (PVD)**.

• Examples include ice melting into water.
 
 
 
• **Solidification**__
 __
 
• **Solidification** is the process of changing from a **liquid to a solid** state.
